description:
Factory AI GMO's commercial platform needs an account/identity record for the people who sign up to use it — the foundation everything else in the commercial platform (Organizations, Projects, factory runs, billing) is built on. This module intentionally comes before Organizations: an Organization needs an owner, and no owner can exist until this module does. This is the second module of Factory AI GMO's own Commercial App, built by the Software Construction Factory itself.

This platform is NOT single-product. A table named 'users' (columns include companyId, clientId, employeeId, appProfile, enabledModules, qrCode) and a linking table 'userCompanies' already exist live in this database, and they are shared, cross-product infrastructure, not POS-specific: this same factory already has host_architect_agent profiles for 'pos' and 'loans' (SmartLoans), real posReward* modules, and real Arcade PRDs (examples/prd_arcade*.json — wallet, game, chip pack, transaction). The live 'users' table's own appProfile column has real production values like 'loans', confirming an established, already-used pattern: one shared identity table, scoped per product line via appProfile/enabledModules, rather than a separate identity table per product.

This makes the identity question for Factory GMO/the commercial platform a genuinely open one, not a closed one: should a Factory AI GMO account be a NEW appProfile value on the EXISTING shared users table (following the platform's own established pattern for onboarding a new product line — pos, loans, and presumably rewards/arcade all did this), or does Factory GMO warrant a separate identity system because it's a different kind of product (a B2B software-generation service consumed by developers/businesses, not a consumer- or retail-facing app like the others)? See Open Architectural Question #1 — this PRD deliberately does not answer it.

BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS
- A visitor can create a new account by providing an email, full name, and password, without being authenticated first (there is no account to authenticate as, yet).
- Each account is uniquely identified by its email address.
- An account has a verification state, since a real signup flow needs to know whether the email address has actually been confirmed.
- An account has a lifecycle status (e.g. active, suspended, deleted), mirroring the same convention used for Organization.
- An authenticated account holder can view and update their own profile (full name; email/password changes are more sensitive and are explicitly out of scope for this PRD — see Open Design Questions).

CONSTRAINTS — already decided, satisfy them rather than re-deciding them
- Passwords must never be stored, logged, or returned in plaintext, anywhere, under any circumstance — only a server-computed hash is ever persisted. This applies to every log statement (application, error, audit) as well as every API response, not just the database column.
- The public signup endpoint must not accept or be able to set emailVerified, status, or any other internal-only field from the request body — only email, fullName, and a password are legitimate signup inputs.
- Whatever the Architect decides for Open Question #1, a Factory GMO account must never be given a POS GMO companyId (a companyId represents a POS GMO retail tenant; a Factory GMO account is not one) — this is settled regardless of whether the identity table itself is shared or separate.

OPEN ARCHITECTURAL QUESTIONS — deliberately unresolved; do not silently pick an answer and hide the ambiguity
1. Shared vs. separate identity: should this account be a new row in the existing, shared 'users' table (a new appProfile value, e.g. 'factory', following the platform's own established multi-product pattern), or does it need its own separate table? Both are legitimate given what already exists in this codebase — decide and justify, don't default silently either way. If reusing 'users', account for the fact that its existing columns (companyId, clientId, employeeId, qrCode) are meaningless for a Factory GMO account and must not be forced to hold fake/placeholder values.
2. Authentication mechanism: this PRD asks only for the account *record* to exist and for signup (account creation) to work. How login actually works — session tokens, JWT, cookies, expiry, refresh — is not specified here and must not be invented as a side effect of this PRD. Treat 'a signup endpoint exists' and 'a login/session system exists' as two separate architectural decisions.
3. Email verification mechanism: this module records whether an email is verified, but the actual mechanism (verification email, token/link, expiry) is not specified. Do not invent an email-sending flow as a side effect of this PRD.
4. Password reset / change flow: not specified here. A change-password or forgot-password endpoint is a separate, future decision.
5. Duplicate signup: what happens when someone signs up with an email that already has an account? The concrete policy (reject with a specific error vs. something else) is an open question for the Architect/Database/Backend agents to decide and justify — the same category of question duplicate-lead handling was for leadCapture (see ADR-002), but sharper here, since an account's email must be unique by definition, not merely deduplicated by policy.
6. Password hashing algorithm and work factor: left to the Backend Agent to choose a secure, current default; not prescribed here.

This PRD intentionally leaves schema shape, relationships, and endpoints beyond what's named above to the Architect/Database/Backend agents to determine — consistent with the commercialization plan's own instruction that the exact modules and schema should be discovered and designed by the Software Factory from the commercial requirements, not assumed in advance.

fields.name: email
fields.description: Unique identifier for this account. Must be normalized consistently (case/whitespace) wherever it is compared or stored, since duplicate-signup handling (see Open Design Questions) depends on that normalization being applied the same way everywhere.

fields.name: passwordHash
fields.description: Server-computed password hash only. The public signup endpoint must never accept, store, log, or return a plaintext password. Hashing algorithm and work factor are left to the Backend Agent to choose a secure, current default.

fields.name: emailVerified
fields.description: Whether this account's email has been verified. Defaults to false on signup. The verification mechanism itself is an open design question, not specified here.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Account lifecycle state, e.g. active, suspended, deleted. Defaults to active on creation. Transition rules are an open design question, not specified here.

endpoints.description: Public, unauthenticated endpoint that creates a new account. Must reject requests missing email, fullName, or password. Must hash the password server-side before persisting it and must never store, log, or return the plaintext password. Must not accept emailVerified, status, or any other internal-only field from the request body. Must validate and normalize the email. Must apply some form of abuse mitigation (rate limiting and/or spam/bot filtering) appropriate for an unauthenticated, internet-facing account-creation endpoint -- the specific technique is an open design question, not prescribed here. Must handle the case where the email already has an account (see Open Design Questions) with a real, specific, deliberate policy, not a silent duplicate row. Error responses must not leak internal implementation details.
